summary: Iron-framed rear range light at Old Road Bay, Baltimore County, lit 1886 with its front partner, automated in 1929 and still active.

lens.note: Original fourth-order locomotive-type headlight, since replaced by a DCB 24 (NRHP 2002)

structures.material: iron skeleton frame around a wooden tower sheathed in corrugated iron, on brick and stone piers

staffing.note: Sources differ on the end of resident keepers: 1922 (archive, LighthouseFriends), 1929 (nomination: manned until automation), 1933 (Chapter timeline and page)

access.note: Inside the Sparrows Point steel plant grounds, reached by Sparrows Point Boulevard; site and tower closed to the public.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (federally owned per 2002 nomination)

events.note: Work on the rear beacon and dwelling began in September 1885 after $25,000 was appropriated for range lights
Both range lights first shown 15 January 1886, with a fourth-order locomotive-type headlight
Brick walks laid between buildings; plank walk to the water's edge; minor repairs
Iron oil house for 55 five-gallon cans erected at the Cutoff Channel range rear
Illuminant changed from acetylene to oil (Bulletin)
Keeper A. L. Davis towed a disabled motor boat with three aboard into Jones Creek, 13 December 1919
Keeper A. L. Davis towed a disabled seaplane into Jones Creek
Last keeper transferred to the Annapolis depot (archive and LighthouseFriends); the nomination and the Chapter give later end dates
Electrified in June 1929 with commercial current, astronomic clock and relay switch; the nomination ends the manned period at automation in 1929
Keeper's dwelling torn down in the 1920s
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2002
Both upper range lights re-lamped with LED light fixtures

corrections.proposed: iron skeleton frame around a wooden tower sheathed in corrugated iron, on brick and stone piers
corrections.why: The 2002 nomination describes an iron exoskeleton frame around an inner wooden tower on brick and stone piers. Nothing in the sources read describes the tower as brick.

The Chapter gives the rear light as a 70-foot (21.3 m) iron skeleton frame. The 75-foot and 74-foot figures are the light's elevation above the water, not the tower height. No source read supports 27.5 m.

The Chapter's 2014 and 2021 notes give a fixed red light 24 hours a day, and the 1930 Bulletin describes a red light. The nomination says the original light was white. A current Light List check is still needed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive's place record for 'Craighill Channel Upper Rear' gives Fort Howard and a position about 4.4 km from the station. The nomination, LighthouseFriends and the Chapter place this light at Old Road Bay, and the Bulletins' 'Cutoff Channel Range Rear' is the same light. The name match is taken as this station. Bulletins naming 'Craighill Channel Range Rear' (for example the 1914 keeper Harry H. Wills) concern the lower rear light, not this one.

notes_for_editor: Identity: the archive place record for 'Craighill Channel Upper Rear' gives Fort Howard and a position 4.4 km from the station (39 deg 11 min, 76 deg 26 min); the nomination, LighthouseFriends and the Chapter give Old Road Bay, 39.2162, -76.4627, which matches the record's coordinates. The archive keeper roster is matched by name. Ends of keeping: archive Davis to 1922 and Green to 1918; LighthouseFriends Green to 1919; Chapter Green 'at least 1918' and Davis 'at least 1921'; nomination manned to automation in 1929; Chapter: kept keeper until 1933. Automation: 1929 (nomination, Chapter timeline, the 1930 Bulletin's June 1929 electrification). Chapter timeline gives a 1907 tower renovation and a 2009 National Register nomination; neither is in the nomination, so neither is used (the nomination's form is dated 2002). Chapter timeline also gives 70-foot tower. Record range of 80 nm and the focal height 22.6 m: 22.6 m matches 74 feet; the range is not supported by any source read and is not used. The 1914 Bulletin's 'Harry H. Wills, keeper of Craighill Channel Range Rear' concerns the lower rear light (see the sibling lower-rear record) and is not used for this station. The Board reports of 1885 and 1886 are cited only as the nomination quotes them. The 1915 Bulletin illuminant change and the 1921 seaplane date ('October 5' in the OCR) are not used beyond the year, because the OCR scrambles the two columns. The Chapter's 2014 page says the light was re-lamped in 2021 with LED fixtures; the characteristic in the record (Iso W 6s) is not supported. John Peterson: the Chapter biography contains a 1914 injury story that conflicts with its 1915 death, so only the career and death lines are used. Find a Grave lists another John Peterson (1846 to 1915); not linked. Roster person slugs came from roster.py --json. The Bulletin's 1915 and 1921 entries are cited for the year only. The story does not say that no wreck or storm damage is recorded at the rear light: the sources read name none.
